generated one. Other documents REFERENCE this file, or say nothing.
ONE-TRUTH-1 made 19 copies machine-written and machine-checked. That was the wrong shape: a
generated copy is still a copy, it still has to be kept in step, and a reader who finds one has
no way to know whether it is the truth or a stale rendering of it. ONE-TRUTH-2 (the owner's
order) deleted all 19. Where a document's argument needed the reader to know a fingerprint
EXISTS, it now points here; where it did not, the mention was removed.
WHERE A CURRENT VALUE MAY STILL APPEAR, and nowhere else:
- this file
- docs/TAGS.md — the tag register. A tag's hash is what it was when the tag was cut.
- reports/ — the lab journal. Append-only by rule: a report records what was true on the day
it was written and must never be rewritten. Listed as a PREFIX rather than 112 filenames,
which is a decision: enumerating them would be noise that nobody would maintain, and the
append-only rule already makes every one of them history by construction.
TO RE-MINT: run the role's `reproduce` command, put the new value here, and commit. There is
nothing else to update — that is the point.
WHICH DOCUMENT OWNS WHAT, resolved because four of them implied they owned this:
- THIS FILE owns the CURRENT VALUES. Nothing else does.
- docs/SIM.md owns the LINEAGE — which change moved which value to which. Its head points here.
- reports/parity/REBASELINE.md owns WHAT MOVED each one, and now carries no values.
- docs/SHIP-CEREMONY.md owns the PROCEDURE for minting.

camera.covers: the DIRECTOR's decisions: state, phase, anchor, zoom, offsets, camT, targets — INCLUDING the ending the director composes after the last crossing (CAMERA-ENDING-WINDOW-1)
camera.mintedBy: LEADER-LATERAL-BUILD-1 — THE OWNER JUDGED THE BUILD ON A PRODUCTION BUILD (3dc061f4) ON 2026-08-26 AND ACCEPTED IT: space-sprint looks right to him. This hash is that acceptance written down. THE RULE, in his words: the camera holds the corridor centreline and steps aside laterally ONLY when the leader would otherwise be clipped, and only as far as needed; as soon as he fits from the centreline again it returns. WHY IT NEEDED MORE THAN THE OBVIOUS ONE-LINE CHANGE, measured before anything was built: adding the leader to `_applyLateralGuarantee`'s subject list changes the answer on 0 of 2,019 frames, for two independent reasons — the corridor edges are ALWAYS in that list and `lateralShiftToFit` intersects intervals, so a subject lying INSIDE them can never narrow the answer; and the corridor does not fit the frame on 100% of LEADER_ZOOM frames, which pins the helper permanently in its 'split the difference' branch, decided by the extremes alone. So the leader gets his OWN interval from the new `lateralAdmissibleForBody` — his four DRAWN BODY corners against the real frame — and the corridor's answer is CLAMPED into it; when it already keeps him whole the clamp is inert, which is 90.27% of frames. NO EASING WAS ADDED AND NONE WAS NEEDED: the rule moves the pan TARGET, and the existing first-order pan smoother is what turns a target step into a travel, so the 130.6 px 'jolt' LEADER-LATERAL-MINIMAL-1 measured never reaches the picture — a second smoother on one quantity is what this project has twice had to undo. TWO KEYS, both read off a sweep rather than chosen: `leaderLateralMarginPx` budgets for the smoother's residual trailing (without it the rule reports 'he fits' on 383 of the 394 frames that still clipped, because the promise is made at the target and broken before it is drawn — the same job `innerFramePct` does for every other subject), and `leaderLateralMaxPx` bounds the step: identical to unbounded on all four affected tracks, yet load-bearing, because a frame-rectangle test once drove this mechanism 500 world px off the centreline chasing a loss no sideways move could reach. Past the bound he stays PARTLY CLIPPED, deliberately — partial clipping is the lesser evil against a camera that swings. MEASURED, 10 tracks x 10 races per arm, 140,740 LEADER_ZOOM mid-race frames each: clip rate 4.18% -> 1.29% pooled (space-sprint 15.4% -> 3.3%, seatrack 6.5% -> 2.2%, river-run 4.6% -> 0.3%, mountainstreet 4.4% -> 0.8%); the six calm tracks are unchanged because their clipping was never sideways. THE PICTURE DID NOT MOVE: 93 of 100 races carry a >=120 px single-frame movement in BOTH arms, and the largest median change anywhere is 10.07 -> 10.15 px. STILL OPEN and deliberately not in this piece: the along-track residual (830 frames, unchanged by design — it belongs to the ZOOM guarantee, not the pan), and the corridor measuring its own room from `anchorScreenPoint` while `resolveCamera` centres the target, a median 132 px apart.

camera.supersededMintedBy: SHIP-RUNIN-CALM-1 — THE OWNER JUDGED THE RUN-IN ON A PRODUCTION BUILD ON 2026-08-26 AND ACCEPTED IT: the closing phase is calm. This hash is that acceptance written down. TWO REPAIRS, EACH WITH ITS CAUSE FOUND BEFORE IT WAS BUILT. (1) RUNIN-PIVOT-SCOPE-1 — the aim was RESOLVED at the previous frame's zoom and DRAWN at this one's, because `_setTrackTargets` answered how WIDE and where to AIM in one pass while the frame's zoom was settled afterwards. Split at the seam that already existed: `_resolvePanTarget()` now runs after `update()` has settled the zoom on every path. That deleted two of the five compensating corrections the file carried. THE TWO ZOOM-ABOUT-THE-ANCHOR PIVOTS STAY and are bounded on both sides — deleting them costs 59 px -> 360 px of sideways jump (RUNIN-ORDER-FIX-1 measured it and stopped that piece), widening them to the entry path costs the level-set guarantee 48 cut frames. (2) RUNIN-EASED-ADMIT-1 — the level ceiling had no continuity contract at any of its three boundaries: it admitted by a member's full demand in one frame; its ease anchored ONCE and re-projected any target change by the elapsed fraction (river-run seed 18, ceiling 1.3703 -> 2.4251, x1.77, WHILE the ease was already running); and it was DROPPED outright when the run-in stopped composing (mountainstreet seed 32, guaranteed 1.3139 -> 4.0, x3.05, at the crossing). `preLevel` is smooth across every one of those frames, so the discontinuity was never the demand's own. One rule now: re-anchor whenever the target moves, ease both directions in log space over the same `runInOpenMs`, and leave by ARRIVING rather than vanishing. NO KEY WAS ADDED BY ANY OF IT. RESULT, in the unit he can picture: the largest single-frame movement of the picture at the frame corner falls from 580.58 px to 9.73 px on river-run seed 18 and 368.65 -> 10.05 on seed 13; the largest sideways movement of the subject falls from 59.07 px to under 1.5 px; and ZERO of 100 races carry a movement the strand's own rule calls noticeable, where two did. CONFIRMED ON TEN TRACKS, TEN RACES EACH, INCLUDING GARDEN-PATH — excluded from every previous corpus because the harness could not finish it, and now the CALMEST of the ten at 13.05 px. Three fast tracks (space-sprint 66.69 px seed 2, city-circuit 35.34, ice-track 35.21) are recorded as an OPEN QUESTION rather than averaged in: they are the endgame schedule's own closing rate, not the level ceiling, and they fail the >5x-median half of the perceptibility rule. WORLD AND WORLD-OFF WERE MEASURED, NOT ARGUED, and both came back byte-identical (bc01b74fd4f3cfc8 / daf78ff18eca83c6), which is the check that a run-in repair touches no race.
